label: D1 after rare a2->S1 visit, larger if unrewarded and when belief favours S2
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == 1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == -1) * belief_lo
explanation: Active only at D1 (zero at GO/D2). Magnitude is set by the previous trial: large after a rare a2->S1 transition (about +3.8 above baseline if unrewarded, about +2 if rewarded), small residual activity otherwise and slightly below baseline after any S2 visit. Within a2->S1 trials it is higher when the ideal-observer belief favours S2 (negative belief_lo weight); after a1 S1 u it also grows when belief leans S2; on window-first trials (previous unknown) belief_lo stands in. The three previous-trial terms alone give dev R^2 0.68 beyond timing; adding belief terms gives test R^2 0.70 beyond timing (all-observed ceiling 0.77, all 0.87). The upcoming choice adds nothing (dev +0.001). Compared with the earlier value/policy explanation (policy decile ref 0.68), observed-only quantities lose essentially nothing; the remaining gap is mainly window-first trials with unknown history and variable firing after a1 S1 u.

issues: The claimed terms leave a systematic error on test, not scattered noise. Misses show D1 over-predicted by about 0.45 after every S2 trial (a1 S2 u -0.447, a1 S2 r -0.447, a2 S2 r -0.446, a2 S2 u -0.427) and under-predicted after a1 S1 u (+0.375). The term set has no S2 indicator, and its prev_state==1 term (-0.26) pushes the wrong cells, so it never models the below-baseline level after S2 that the explanation itself describes.

The claimed set (test R^2 beyond timing 0.702) does worse than the plain 'last trial' reference table (0.74). A simpler 4-indicator set does better: D1*a2S1u, D1*a2S1r, D1*S2, D1*a1S1r gives 0.735 test.
The explanation leaves out that the feature also sits below baseline after a1 S1 r (residual -0.459; fitted weight -0.45). After an S1 visit, only a1 S1 u stays at baseline (-0.007).

The '+3.8 vs +2' effect sizes match the residual table (+3.39 / +1.74). But in the claimed fit both indicators get nearly the same weight (2.29 vs 2.22): the r/u difference is carried by the shared belief_lo term, so the terms do not encode the size claims directly.

Claims that hold up: firing is D1-only (GO/D2 residuals are exactly 0). The peak is after rare a2->S1, larger when unrewarded. Belief has a negative weight (higher when belief favours S2). Dropping the next-choice future term costs nothing.

Once the S2 and a1 S1 r levels are modelled, the remaining phase x previous-trial errors are all below 0.08 in size. The largest is D1 on first-of-window trials ('?'), -0.08. So the claimed 'uneven a1 S1 u firing' residual was mostly an artefact of the term choice.
